headline: If Something Happened To You Tonight, Would Your Family Know Where To Start?
lead: A complete digital binder for every password, policy, account and critical detail your family would need — so they’re not left scrambling when they need it most.
caption: “I realized I was the single point of failure for my family.”

story.title: The “Nobody Else Knows” Moment
paragraphs: You’re doing something completely ordinary. Paying the mortgage. Looking for an insurance document.
Then the thought hits you:
“If something happened to me, nobody would even know this needed doing.”
And the realization follows: I’m the one who knows.
Your spouse doesn’t know your phone passcode. He doesn’t know where your life insurance policy is filed. He wouldn’t know which account pays your mortgage, or how to access your utility bills.
“If something happened to me tonight, my husband would have to start sorting all of this, and he doesn’t even know which bank I use.”
It’s a heavy, invisible load. The responsibility you never meant to carry alone could leave absolute chaos behind when the people you love need it least.
You’ve been meaning to sort it out for years, but life simply gets in the way.

alternatives.title: The uncomfortable truth we secretly know

items.title: “I’ll do it later”
paragraphs: But later never comes. Meanwhile, there are more accounts, more policies, more documents — and that background anxiety grows louder.

items.title: Scattered Notes
paragraphs: Passwords in your phone notes. Documents in “that drawer.”
This isn’t a system. It’s a scavenger hunt for your family.

items.title: Notes Apps
paragraphs: Disorganised, and usually just turns into the Netflix password and a grocery list.
Not secure. Not structured. Not enough.

items.title: The Expensive Lawyer
paragraphs: $2,000+ and it covers the legal side.
But it doesn’t tell your husband how to pay the water bill or what the Wi-Fi password is.

alternatives.close:
The problem isn’t that you don’t care about your family. This is how you got into this situation in the first place.
The problem is that there’s never been a simple, complete system designed specifically for this purpose.

solution.title: What if everything they needed was in one place?
paragraphs: Not another list you have to create yourself.
A simple, complete system that walks you through what matters, gives everything a place, and leaves your family with one place to look if they ever need it.
No guessing what you've forgotten. No information scattered across drawers, phones and folders.
Just one complete map of the things they would need to know.
